rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The midpoint temperature leaves room to probe selectivity in either direction.

All pairs have excess resolution, so halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed reveals how the critical pairs respond to gradient steepness.

The critical cluster responds strongly to gradient duration. A 14-minute gradient should recover much of its resolution while keeping the last peak near or below the apparent 10-minute time-penalty threshold.

Only one pair remains below baseline resolution. Raising temperature while holding the gradient fixed tests whether selectivity can resolve that pair and further shorten retention without a time penalty.

The central cluster appears to have undergone an elution-order crossover between 40 and 50 C. A further 5 C increase may separate the crossed pair sufficiently while preserving resolution elsewhere and keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

At 55 C the formerly critical pair appears to have reversed order, so a slightly steeper gradient may now improve its separation. Shortening the gradient to 12 minutes tests this while reducing retention time, with some resolution margin in the neighboring pairs.

Injection 6 has reached the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Slightly reducing the gradient slope tests a nearby method that may retain the maximum score while improving separation of the other close pair.

The maximum CRF is already secured. Test higher temperature to strengthen separation of the crossover pair, coupled with a shallower gradient to protect the neighboring pair while targeting a last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Return to the best temperature and test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to probe selectivity in the two close pairs. Injection 6 remains the maximum-score benchmark; this run explores whether that score can be retained with a shifted gradient window.

Lengthening injection 9's gradient should bring the earlier close pair above R = 1.5 while retaining sufficient separation in the later pair. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, potentially giving another maximum-score method with better resolution margin.
